scripts/npu_op_probe.py emits 6 minimal per-operator ONNX graphs into artifacts/npu_op_probe/ with a manifest. Hand-authored via onnx.helper rather than torch-exported so a cixbuild failure is attributable to exactly one operator. Verified known-good before use: all 6 pass onnx.checker full_check, all 6 execute under onnxruntime 1.28 with finite outputs, and the causal conv is verified genuinely causal (perturbing the last timestep leaves earlier outputs bit-identical). README documents the cixbuild invocation and how to record results, including the silent-CPU-fallback case which looks like success and performs like failure.

AUDIT COMPLETE on x86 host with no board. Headline: every arithmetic operator GDN needs is natively supported (CumSum -> ArmCumulate, delta rule -> ArmMatMul/ArmEltwise, causal conv -> ArmDepthwiseConv), but the sequential recurrence is NOT expressible - Scan rejected outright, Loop accepted only with a compile-time-constant trip count via silent static unrolling (no loop survives in the IR), Loop with runtime trip count rejected ('Graph is not DAG'). Empirically confirms the CPU-first mapping: keeping the scan on CPU is not a preference, the NPU has no construct for it. Also surfaced two undocumented environment facts (cixbuilder wheel is cp310-only; cixparse imports tensorflow even for ONNX). Written up in docs/FINDINGS.md 1 with logs committed under artifacts/npu_op_probe/audit/. Caveat: frontend lowering only - per-op NPU-vs-CPU placement and throughput still need full cixbuild and on-device runs (ob-8xc).

ADR 0003 written. Primary Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, fallback Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B, decided against config.json read directly from HF rather than the survey summary. Confirmed from primary source: 4B is 32 layers = exactly 24 GDN + 8 full attention with an explicit layer_types array, hidden 2560, 262144 native context, 16/32 linear key/value heads, 128/128 head dims, conv kernel 4. Computed the memory decomposition: GDN state 48MB flat at every context length vs KV cache 128MB@4K rising to 8GB@262K, and an all-full-attention counterfactual of ~32.8GB at 262K, so the hybrid saves ~24.8GB (75%) on a 64GB board. Caught and corrected a figure I had been repeating: the 4B has 32 value heads so its per-layer state is 524,288 floats, not the 262,144 from the GDN-2 paper's 1.3B config. One assumption flagged as open: the n_v_heads x d_k x d_v layout still needs confirming from modeling code (ob-37v).

bench/manifest.py implemented. capture() / write() / manifest_ref() plus a __main__ that dumps the current machine's manifest. Stdlib-only (imports cleanly in the NOE 3.10 env and on the board). Captures run_id, UTC timestamp, git SHA + dirty flag, host CPU model/kernel/core count, per-CPU cpufreq max/min/governor/cpu_capacity (the big.LITTLE hook for Cortex-A720 big/medium/A520 little), aarch64 ISA features parsed from /proc/cpuinfo (sve/sve2/i8mm/bf16/asimddp/sme - needed to know which of our SVE/NEON/scalar paths actually ran), thermal zones, meminfo, python and optional package versions via importlib.metadata without importing them, plus a caller passthrough for compiler flags and dispatch path.

Every probe is individually guarded so capture() never raises - a manifest failure must not take down a benchmark run. Verified on x86: runs clean, and correctly distinguishes not-applicable (isa_features null on x86_64) from empty (thermal_zones [] where /sys/class/thermal exists but has no zones) from probe-failed (cpufreq nulls in this VM). ruff check and format clean.

ADR 0004 ratifies the descope ladder as dated, operable decision points with observable triggers for T-4 (Aug 10) through T-1 (Aug 13).

Its most valuable output is a number the original ladder did not have: the board's USEFULNESS CUTOFF is 2026-08-08, two days EARLIER than the T-4 abandonment trigger. The ADR separates two questions PLAN.md section 7 conflated - when we stop pursuing a board versus the last date one could arrive and still change the submission. Even a minimal on-device addendum is ~3 days hardware plus ~1 day write-up integration; counting back from the Aug 13 EOD internal target gives Aug 9, and one day of padding for bring-up friction already observed twice on the compiler side gives Aug 8. A full heterogeneous NPU+GPU+CPU submission needed the board by ~Aug 4, which has passed. So if T-4 fires as written on Aug 10, the useful window had already closed two days earlier.

Honest verdict recorded: a board-free Edge AI submission clears PLAN.md section 8's minimum-viable bar outright on hardware-independent work already done, and plausibly reaches target tier since the phone hedge keeps a real Vulkan GPU leg - only the NPU clause is lost. It cannot compete for Physical AI. Also flagged that zero benchmark numbers exist anywhere yet, so the board-free MVP is currently a credible plan rather than a credible result.
